question: Should OpenClaw permanently support plugin-authored AI-safety events plus durable, operator-queryable safety history as core plugin SDK and Gateway contracts?
rationale: The branch is technically substantial and security-aware, but accepting a public plugin capability, manifest permission, persistent storage, RPCs, CLI, and UI is a product and compatibility commitment that implementation review cannot safely make.

options.title: Approve the complete public contract
options.body: Accept `safetyDiagnostics.emit()`, `safetyEventTypes`, persistent event history, and operator query surfaces as supported APIs, then require focused compatibility and retention documentation before merge.

options.title: Land a narrower internal seam first
options.body: Keep core-owned event emission and exporter plumbing, while deferring the public plugin emission API, manifest permission, and broad operator surface to a separately sponsored design.

options.title: Decline this core direction
options.body: Do not add the permanent core contracts; retain the idea for a plugin-owned or future diagnostics design if maintainers want it later.

recommendation.title: Land a narrower internal seam first
recommendation.body: Keep core-owned event emission and exporter plumbing, while deferring the public plugin emission API, manifest permission, and broad operator surface to a separately sponsored design.
